ruled_out_vectors.title: Swap math rounding direction — all operations favor pool
ruled_out_vectors.description: Exhaustive per-function analysis of SwapMath.computeSwapByInputStep, computeSwapByOutputStep, SqrtPriceMath, and FeeHelper confirms ALL 15+ arithmetic operations round in the pool's favor. Input swaps: fee calculation rounds UP, amount out rounds DOWN. Output swaps: amount in rounds UP, fee rounds UP. The single exception (exchange fee in FeeHelper.L186 rounds DOWN for input swaps) only affects a third-party fee recipient, not pool solvency.
evidence: SwapMath.sol L53-84: input swap step math in unchecked, feeAmount=mulDivRoundingUp (L65)
SwapMath.sol L109-150: output swap step math in unchecked, amountIn=mulDivRoundingUp (L138-140)
SqrtPriceMath.sol: getNextSqrtPriceFromInput uses conservative rounding, getNextSqrtPriceFromOutput moves price further
FeeHelper.sol L186: exchange fee input rounds DOWN (favors user) but fee goes to external recipient, not pool
DynamicHelper.sol L406: feeGrowthGlobalX128 uses floor division, dust stays in pool
AMMModule.sol L1665: expectedProtocolFee uses floor, more goes to LP

ruled_out_vectors.title: Balance verification prevents phantom reserves from fee-on-transfer tokens
ruled_out_vectors.description: _collectToken (L2913-2920) uses strict equality: `balanceOf(this) != balanceBefore + amount -> revert`. This prevents fee-on-transfer tokens from creating phantom reserves. Similarly, _finalizeSwapCollectFundsAndDisburse (L2208) checks `balanceInBefore + amountIn != balanceInAfter -> revert`. Both checks prevent any token behavior from creating a discrepancy between tracked and actual balances.
evidence: AMMModule.sol L2913-2920: _collectToken strict balance check
AMMModule.sol L2206-2210: swap finalization strict balance check
Test: test_C25_fee_on_transfer_token_addLiquidity_reverts confirms revert

ruled_out_vectors.title: Reentrancy guard preserves ENTERED bit during queued hook fee processing
ruled_out_vectors.description: _executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers (L3183) calls _setReentrancyFlags(NO_FLAGS) at L3190, but the _setReentrancyFlags function (TstorishReentrancyGuardWithFlags.sol L68-72) preserves the ENTERED bit: `currentGuard = _getTstorish(...) & ENTERED`. This means only custom flags (SWAP_GUARD_FLAG, LIQUIDITY_GUARD_FLAG, etc.) are cleared for proper queue processing, while the core reentrancy guard remains active. Any nonReentrant/nonReentrantWithFlags function will still revert on reentry.
evidence: AMMModule.sol L3190: _setReentrancyFlags(NO_FLAGS)
TstorishReentrancyGuardWithFlags.sol L68-72: preserves ENTERED bit
TstorishReentrancyGuardWithFlags.sol L78-81: _nonReentrantBefore checks ENTERED
ModuleFeeCollection.sol L72-82: collectHookFeesByHook checks flags, not nonReentrant
AMMModule.sol L3127-3139: _transferHookFeesByHook uses decrement-before-transfer pattern

ruled_out_vectors.title: Flash loan balance-based verification prevents profit extraction
ruled_out_vectors.description: Flash loan (_flashLoan L3288-3382) records pre-loan balances, transfers the loan, executes callback, then verifies balance >= pre-balance + fee. Surplus is converted to protocol fees. The verification is balance-based (not reserve-based), so it cannot be manipulated via pool state. Fee calculation uses mulDivRoundingUp ensuring the protocol always charges at least the computed fee.
evidence: AMMModule.sol L3308-3315: requiredTokenBalanceAfter = balanceBefore + feeAmount
AMMModule.sol L3334-3346: post-callback balance check with surplus to protocolFees
AMMModule.sol L3300: feeAmount = mulDivRoundingUp(loanAmount, flashLoanBPS, MAX_BPS)
Test: test_C9_flash_loan_no_profit, test_hyp11_flash_loan_fee_inflation

ruled_out_vectors.title: Fee conservation equation holds across all swap paths
ruled_out_vectors.description: Complete fee lifecycle trace from input to output for both swap types confirms: user_pays = amountIn_to_pool + exchangeFee + protocolExchangeFee + feeOnTop + protocolFeeOnTop + hookFees_net + protocolFee_from_hooks. Each component maps to exactly one storage location (reserves, feeBalance, protocolFees, tokensOwed). No double-counting or missing fees found. Output swap hook fees correctly increase pool output requirement (not decrease user output), maintaining conservation.
evidence: AMMModule.sol L2598-2677: _applySwapByInputInputFees hooks bounded by swapAmountIn check
AMMModule.sol L2699-2743: _applySwapByInputOutputFees output hooks bounded
AMMModule.sol L2851-2895: _applySwapByOutputOutputFees ADDS hook fees to output requirement
AMMModule.sol L1654-1677: _validateProtocolFees reserveIn = amountIn - totalFees
FeeHelper.sol L42-136: Both input/output fee calculation functions conserve total
Tests: test_C6_solvency_after_swap_add_remove, test_C6_solvency_with_exchange_fees, testFuzz_C6

ruled_out_vectors.title: Protocol fee BPS validation prevents unchecked math underflow
ruled_out_vectors.description: _setProtocolFees (L3458-3468) validates all three BPS fields <= MAX_BPS. _setTokenFee (L3485-3491) validates hopFeeBPS < MAX_BPS (strict). setExchangeProtocolFeeOverride (L87-93) validates protocolFeeBPS > MAX_BPS leads to revert. The concern about FeeHelper.sol L161/L223 unchecked subtraction underflow when protocolFeeBPS > MAX_BPS is ruled out by these input validations.
evidence: AMMModule.sol L3458-3461: _setProtocolFees validates all three > MAX_BPS
AMMModule.sol L3486: _setTokenFee validates >= MAX_BPS
ModuleAdmin.sol L91-93: setExchangeProtocolFeeOverride validates > MAX_BPS
FeeHelper.sol L161: unchecked feeOnTopAmount - protocolFeeAmount safe when BPS <= MAX_BPS
FeeHelper.sol L223: unchecked feeAmount - protocolFeeAmount safe when BPS <= MAX_BPS

ruled_out_vectors.title: Token owed / fee debt fallback maintains solvency invariant
ruled_out_vectors.description: When _distributeOrCollectLiquidityToken (L1282-1304) encounters a failed ERC20 transfer, it stores the amount as tokensOwed (L1300) via _storeTokensOwed. The fee balance was already decremented. The tokens remain in the contract's actual balance. The tokensOwed mapping tracks the debt. Solvency invariant: balance >= reserves + feeBalance + protocolFees + tokensOwed continues to hold because the reserve/fee decrement equals the tokensOwed increment, and the balance doesn't change (transfer failed). collectTokensOwed zeros debt before transfer, preventing double-collection.
evidence: AMMModule.sol L1298-1301: failed transfer leads to _storeTokensOwed
AMMModule.sol L2937-2960: _storeTokensOwed with overflow check
AMMModule.sol L3045-3060: _transferTokensOwed zeros before transfer
ModuleFeeCollection.sol L46-50: collectTokensOwed is nonReentrant

ruled_out_vectors.title: Round-trip swap always loses money due to fees + price impact
ruled_out_vectors.description: Both unit tests and fuzz tests confirm: executing swap A to B then B to A always results in the user receiving less than they started with. The loss comes from pool fees (charged both directions) and price impact. Tested with up to 50 tiny swaps and 25 fuzz iterations.
evidence: Test: test_C16_flash_swap_reverse_no_profit 10e18 round-trip loses money
Test: testFuzz_C16_round_trip_no_profit 25 fuzz runs, all lose money
Test: test_C7_no_value_creation_multi_step 4 swaps, no value created
Test: test_hyp10_many_tiny_swaps 50 tiny swaps, solvency maintained

ruled_out_vectors.title: Hook fee key namespace collision impossible (TOKEN_MANAGED_HOOK_FEE = 0x7F vs real addresses)
ruled_out_vectors.description: Hook-managed fees use key hash(hookAddress, hash(tokenFor, tokenFee)). Token-managed fees use hash(TOKEN_MANAGED_HOOK_FEE, hash(tokenFor, tokenFee)) where TOKEN_MANAGED_HOOK_FEE = 0x7F. For a collision, a hook would need address 0x7F, which is in the precompile region and unreachable for contract deployment. The collection functions (collectHookFeesByHook vs collectHookFeesByToken) compute different keys and have different auth checks, preventing cross-path fee theft.
evidence: Constants.sol L59: TOKEN_MANAGED_HOOK_FEE = 0x7F
AMMModule.sol L2978-2988: _storeHookFees key branching
ModuleFeeCollection.sol L72-82: collectHookFeesByHook requires msg.sender == hook
ModuleFeeCollection.sol L103-109: collectHookFeesByToken requires token admin

ruled_out_vectors.title: createPool + addLiquidity reentrancy window is safe
ruled_out_vectors.description: ModuleLiquidity.createPool (L68-101) calls _clearReentrancyGuard() at L79 before delegatecalling addLiquidity. This temporarily sets NOT_ENTERED. However: (1) there is no external call between _clearReentrancyGuard and the delegatecall, (2) the delegatecall to addLiquidity immediately sets ENTERED via its nonReentrantWithFlags modifier, (3) if the delegatecall reverts, the outer createPool function also reverts (L82-85), rolling back the _clearReentrancyGuard change.
evidence: ModuleLiquidity.sol L74: createPool uses nonReentrant
ModuleLiquidity.sol L79: _clearReentrancyGuard() before delegatecall
ModuleLiquidity.sol L81: delegatecall to addLiquidity
ModuleLiquidity.sol L82-85: revert on delegatecall failure

hypotheses_tested.title: tokensOwed desync between position and pool accounting
hypotheses_tested.rationale: tokensOwed uses separate key namespaces (LIQUIDITY_OWED, hook address, TOKEN_MANAGED_HOOK_FEE). Each namespace has distinct write paths and collection paths. Overflow/underflow checks present on all mutations. Fuzz testing confirmed obligations never exceed balance.

hypotheses_tested.title: Rounding asymmetry in add vs remove liquidity paths
hypotheses_tested.rationale: Pool type (DynamicPoolType) delegates to Uniswap V3-style math which consistently rounds against the user (collect less, deposit more). _safeIncrementUint128 and _safeDecrementUint128 prevent over/underflow. Add liquidity followed by remove always results in protocol gaining dust.

hypotheses_tested.title: Many tiny swaps harvesting truncation for profit
hypotheses_tested.rationale: 50 tiny swaps (1e14 each) tested. Fee calculation uses mulDivRoundingUp, so even 1 wei of input produces at least 1 wei of fee. Solvency holds after all tiny operations. The protocol's rounding consistently captures more from the user.

hypotheses_tested.title: Flash loan to inflate fee accumulators
hypotheses_tested.rationale: Flash loans are balance-based, not reserve-based. They don't modify pool reserves, feeBalance, or any pool-specific accounting. Surplus goes to protocol fees. The pool type's fee growth accumulators are only modified during swaps, not flash loans.

overall_assessment: The Limit Break AMM demonstrates exceptionally high code quality for solvency properties. All arithmetic operations in swap math round in the pool's favor. The reentrancy guard (TstorishReentrancyGuardWithFlags) correctly preserves the ENTERED bit while allowing custom flag manipulation for hook fee queue processing. Fee conservation equations hold across all tested paths. Balance verification prevents phantom reserves. No exploitable insolvency vectors found. The protocol's defense-in-depth approach (fee rounding + balance checks + reentrancy guard + overflow protection) makes insolvency extremely difficult to achieve.
